entities.summary: Johann Eberlin von Günzburg was a German theologian and reformer born in 1465 in Kleinkötz, who became prominent as the author of reformist flysheets and pamphlets. His theological works were widely distributed and influenced the Protestant Reformation in Western Europe. The Catholic Church responded by issuing a papal bull, which led to a period of persecution against Protestant writers and thinkers. Despite this, von Günzburg's writings continued to circulate, and he is considered an important figure in the development of Protestant theology. His legacy can be seen in the numerous reformist movements that emerged in the 16th century, and his ideas had a lasting impact on the development of Protestantism in Europe. In 1533, von Günzburg died in Ingolstadt, leaving behind a body of work that continues to be studied by scholars today.
